meaning.zh:
“事先提醒某人” 或 “让某人提前知道”。

这个短语的起源可以追溯到军事领域，在战斗中，士兵会向后方传递即将发生的事情，提醒大家提高警觉。后来，这个表达逐渐进入日常用语，用来表示在事情发生之前对他人进行警告或提醒。
meaning.en: This phrase originates from the military, where soldiers would inform those behind them of imminent actions or events, essentially working as a warning to be alert. Over time, this expression has found its way into everyday language, used to indicate warning or informing someone about something in advance.

lines.en: Thanks for giving me the heads-up about the meeting change.
lines.zh: 谢谢你提前通知我会议时间的变动。

lines.en: I just wanted to give you a heads-up that we might need to work late tonight.
lines.zh: 我只是想提前提醒你，我们今晚可能需要加班。

lines.en: Please give me a heads-up if you need anything else.
lines.zh: 如果你还需要什么，请提前和我说。
